title: Latency Between Every Pair (Floyd-Warshall)
real_world_story: A network monitoring system needs to answer latency queries between any two routers instantly. Rather than running a shortest-path search for every query, the system precomputes the minimum latency between every pair of routers.

real_world_connection.input_represents: Routers and weighted links representing latency in milliseconds
real_world_connection.algorithm_represents: Precomputing the minimum latency between every pair of routers

problem_statement: Given N routers numbered 0 to N-1, E undirected network links each with a latency weight W, and Q queries each asking for the minimum latency between two routers, answer every query. Print -1 if the two routers are not connected.
task: For each query (A, B), print the minimum latency between router A and router B, or -1 if they are not connected.
input_format: The first line contains two integers N and E. The next E lines each contain three integers u v w describing an undirected link between routers u and v with latency w. The next line contains an integer Q. The next Q lines each contain two integers A B representing a query.
output_format: Print Q lines. Each line contains the minimum latency between the queried pair, or -1 if they are not connected.

examples.explanation: 0 to 3: path 0->1->2->3 costs 10+20+15=45. 1 to 3: path 1->2->3 costs 20+15=35. 0 to 1: direct link costs 10.
Routers 0 and 1 are disconnected from routers 2 and 3, so both queries return -1.

expected_algorithm.name: Floyd-Warshall
expected_algorithm.reason: Floyd-Warshall computes the shortest path between every pair of vertices in O(N^3), making it ideal for small networks where many pair queries are expected.

hint: Build an N x N distance matrix initialised to infinity, with dist[i][i] = 0 and direct link weights filled in.
For each intermediate router k, check whether routing through k improves the path between every pair (i, j).
After the algorithm, any dist[A][B] still equal to infinity means the routers are not connected.
real_world_takeaway: Floyd-Warshall is used in small-to-medium networks where all-pairs latency must be precomputed, such as in network simulation tools and latency dashboards.
